description: A bounded snapshot of recent logs from the running stack (default the last 200 lines, at most 10000), returned as text. Read-only: reading with a cursor writes nothing. Not a stream: every JSON line has a `seq`, the response carries `data.nextCursor`, and passing that value back as `after` returns only newer lines (an unchanged log gives no lines and the same cursor; a cursor older than the retained log returns the oldest available lines with `data.truncated: true`). Optionally select the project with projectPath. After a failed `up`, call it first with unhealthy: true to read only the failing or still-starting services. Otherwise use `status` first to find which service is failing, then pass services to narrow the output and source `runtime` to skip image build output and read why it failed. For local-process services, pass run: current, previous or a run id to read one run apart from older ones. CLI equivalent: `flisk logs --json`.

after.description: Only lines with seq greater than this cursor. Pass the data.nextCursor from a previous logs call; it may be a long integer, so send it as a string.

context.description: With grep, keep this many neighboring lines per service (match: false). Default 0.

grep.description: Filter content by plain-text match (meta-characters have no special meaning); ignores case unless the text contains uppercase. Matches have match: true.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the Flisk project root; run this operation from that directory.

run.description: Only one run of each local-process service: current, previous, or a numeric run id. Not available for Docker services.

since.description: Only logs newer than this (real event times), for example 30s, 5m, 1h

source.description: runtime: only what the services printed (where a crash cause such as an exception or a missing variable is); build: only image build steps. Omit for both.

unhealthy.description: Only the logs of failing or still-starting services. The first call after a failed `up`; with every service healthy it returns nothing, not an error.

name: logs
